provided tools, make recovery decisions yourself when the records are
sufficient, and do not ask the user to choose among objectively verifiable
repairs. Stop calling tools once the goal is verified or after 15
model turns.

turns.text:
All goals are verified complete. Here's the summary:

## Recovery Results

| Item | Status |
|------|--------|
| **Purchase Order** `PUR-ORD-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted — preserved |
| **Purchase Receipt** `MAT-PRE-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted — preserved |
| **Purchase Invoice** `ACC-PINV-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted, **Paid**, outstanding $0.00 |
| **Payment Entry** `ACC-PAY-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted (docstatus 1), $4,800.00 allocated to the invoice |
| **Duplicate payments** | ✅ None — exactly one Payment Entry references the invoice |
| **Supplier remittance** | ✅ Delivered exactly once (1 attempt, job `d5ff9bac…` finished successfully) |

### What happened
The `RemoteDisconnected` error occurred *after* the Payment Entry submission had already completed on the server. The payment was submitted, the invoice was reconciled to zero outstanding, and no duplicate payment was created.

The only thing that didn't fire was the supplier remittance webhook — the connection loss prevented the `on_submit` webhook event from enqueuing. I created a single remittance job via `requeue_payment_remittance`, which the idempotent receiver accepted and delivered on the first attempt. No duplicate deliveries exist.

All goals are verified complete. Here's the summary:

## Recovery Results

| Item | Status |
|------|--------|
| **Purchase Order** `PUR-ORD-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted — preserved |
| **Purchase Receipt** `MAT-PRE-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted — preserved |
| **Purchase Invoice** `ACC-PINV-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted, **Paid**, outstanding $0.00 |
| **Payment Entry** `ACC-PAY-2026-00001` | ✅ Submitted (docstatus 1), $4,800.00 allocated to the invoice |
| **Duplicate payments** | ✅ None — exactly one Payment Entry references the invoice |
| **Supplier remittance** | ✅ Delivered exactly once (1 attempt, job `d5ff9bac…` finished successfully) |

### What happened
The `RemoteDisconnected` error occurred *after* the Payment Entry submission had already completed on the server. The payment was submitted, the invoice was reconciled to zero outstanding, and no duplicate payment was created.

The only thing that didn't fire was the supplier remittance webhook — the connection loss prevented the `on_submit` webhook event from enqueuing. I created a single remittance job via `requeue_payment_remittance`, which the idempotent receiver accepted and delivered on the first attempt. No duplicate deliveries exist.
